name: Orbit AI - Phase 1 - Stripe payment to CRM

nodes.name: Stripe webhook
nodes.notes: NEW (brief v2): 'built now in Phase 1 with placeholder credentials, not deferred to Phase 5. Only Telnyx stays deferred.' options.rawBody:true is REQUIRED for the signature check in the next node to work at all - Stripe signs the exact raw request bytes, and if this node re-serializes the parsed JSON body instead of preserving the raw string, every signature check will fail even with a correct webhook secret. UNVERIFIED: whether 'rawBody' is the exact option name/nesting for the installed n8n version, and which expression exposes the raw string afterward ($json.body as a raw string vs $binary.data) - this is the single most likely thing in this entire workflow library to need hand-fixing on import. If it doesn't work as written, the safer fix is architectural, not a tweak: move signature verification into a tiny dedicated serverless function (Netlify Function or Cloudflare Worker, consistent with this repo's 'standalone service, not n8n Code nodes' principle for anything non-trivial) that verifies the signature with Stripe's own SDK and forwards only verified events to this webhook.

nodes.name: Verify signature & classify event
nodes.notes: Implements Stripe's documented signature scheme (t=timestamp,v1=hexHMAC over `${t}.${rawBody}` with the webhook secret) - the algorithm itself is stable public Stripe documentation, but this hasn't been tested against a real Stripe webhook delivery, and depends entirely on the previous node's raw-body assumption holding. ALSO ASSUMES the Checkout Session (or PaymentIntent) was created with metadata.opportunityId set to the Twenty CRM Opportunity ID, the same link-up pattern as the e-sign/Documenso workflow used for its externalId - that metadata has to be set wherever the Stripe payment link/Checkout Session actually gets created (the portal's Onboarding Form step, Netlify-hosted, not built in this repo).

nodes.name: Advance CRM to Live Client
nodes.notes: brief v2 / 05 Section 7 phrases this as one webhook advancing 'Contract Signed -> Onboarding -> Live Client' - ASSUMPTION FLAGGED: this workflow jumps straight to 'Live Client' on payment success rather than pausing at an intermediate 'Onboarding' stage, since the brief doesn't specify a reason to wait once payment clears. If a real intermediate step needs to happen first (e.g. W6.3's onboarding provisioning automation, documented-only/not built), reconsider staging this as Onboarding here and a *second* stage-advance once provisioning actually completes - 'onboardingProvisioningStatus: Pending' is included specifically so that later automation has something to update rather than this workflow silently claiming provisioning is done when it isn't. Same Twenty CRM REST-shape uncertainty as every other workflow here.

nodes.name: Respond: ignored (valid, not relevant)
nodes.notes: Returns 200 for a validly-signed event this workflow doesn't act on, per Stripe's own guidance - responding with an error status to an event you're just not handling causes Stripe to retry it unnecessarily.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: false, reason: 'Invalid Stripe signature.' }) }}
